page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for scratch caching and temporary files, with no discrete GPUs attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong performance in single-threaded compression tasks, with gzip throughput reaching 31.35 GB/sec, placing it in the top performance tier. Single-core processor capabilities register in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1643.0 and a stress-ng score of 1948.38. However, parallel multi-threaded throughput reflects the physical constraints of two execution cores, resulting in lower-tier results on Geekbench multi-core (3707.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (26.0 GB/sec). Memory read bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks measured at 36.24 GB/sec, and Redis operations achieved 5.66 million operations per second, both sitting in the lower performance quartile.

The instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring high memory capacity and fast ephemeral storage without paying for surplus CPU cores. The combination of hardware-level AMX and AVX-512 support with dedicated local NVMe makes it well matched for database engines, Redis or in-memory caching layers, medium-scale ETL operations, and backend web services handling memory-intensive operations.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 32.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside 236 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Single-core processor capabilities are solid, marked by strong single-threaded gzip compression at 31.35 GB/s and average single-core Geekbench ratings. Conversely, multi-threaded parallel throughput and uncached memory read bandwidth land in the lower quartile due to the two-core physical baseline. The bundled high-speed local disk and large memory allocation make the instance a resource-efficient choice for memory-bound applications that do not require heavy thread scaling. Recommended workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching systems, data preprocessing, and containerized enterprise services requiring fast scratch space.
